newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices ease on low consumer demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices ease on low consumer demand.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Thursday fell as consumer demand eased at higher levels while fresh arrivals prompted profit-taking, dealers said.

In the ready delivery sugar S-30 slid by five rupees at 1,285/1,310 rupees per quintal while M-30 fell by 12 rupees at 1,320/1,383 rupees per quintal. Sugar mill delivery fell to 1,210/1,225 rupees per quintal from 1,215/1,235 rupees on fresh offerings by the millers at improved level.

Sugar was up by 20/25 rupees per quintal on Wednesday following a lower than expected quota for next month announced by the government. The free sale quota for April was announced at 700,000 tonnes against market expectation of 750,000 tonnes.
The quota for March is 700,000 tonnes.
"The free sale quota for May is announced at 750,000 tonnes and for June at 800,000 tonnes," one broker said.
